title: Is Love Really Blind?
paragraphs:
Is Love Really Blind?
The Most Dangerous Lies We Believe About Love... and the Savior Who Opens Our Eyes
We've laughed about it at weddings.
We've whispered it when someone ignored every warning sign.
But what if that famous phrase has quietly become one of the most spiritually dangerous ideas of our generation?
What if love was never meant to be blind?
What if sin is what blinds us...
...and love is what finally helps us see?
Because the greatest love story ever written did not begin with two people finding each other.
It began with humanity running away from God.
Long before social media celebrated "following your heart," Scripture warned us about it.
"The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?" (Jeremiah 17:9, ESV)
The Hebrew word translated "deceitful" is עָקֹב (ʿāqōḇ).
It literally carries the idea of something crooked, twisted, or treacherous.
It is capable of convincing us that darkness is light, selfishness is love, compromise is wisdom, and rebellion is freedom.
That is why feelings alone are never trustworthy guides.
"If it feels right, it must be love."
"If you love Me, you will keep My commandments." (John 14:15)
In Greek, Jesus used the word ἀγαπᾶτέ (agapate) from ἀγαπάω (agapaō).
This is not merely emotional affection.
Love that chooses the good of another even when feelings fluctuate.
The world's definition of love often begins with attraction.
That difference explains countless broken relationships.
Many people don't fall in love.
They fall into the desperate hope that another broken person will heal wounds only Christ can restore.
"I must have fallen out of love."
Many simply mistook emotional intoxication for covenantal love.
The Bible never promises endless butterflies.
"Love is patient and kind; love does not envy or boast; it is not arrogant or rude..." (1 Corinthians 13:4–7)
The Greek word for love here is ἀγάπη (agapē).
Agapē is not primarily something you feel.
It is someone you become through Christ.
Real love keeps its eyes open.
And still chooses grace without approving sin.
That is exactly what Jesus did.
The woman caught in adultery stood before religious leaders holding stones.
Everyone was ready to define her by her worst day.
Then He spoke words that continue to echo across history.
"Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more." (John 8:11)
This is the heartbeat of the Gospel.
Perhaps your story doesn't involve adultery.
Anxiety you've buried beneath a smiling face.
A faith that has become routine instead of relationship.
Nothing is beyond His ability to redeem.
"But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us." (Romans 5:8)
The Greek word translated "demonstrates" is συνίστησιν (synistēsin).
It means to prove, establish, or display beyond question.
God did not merely say He loves us.
That is perfect love seeing the very worst...
and willingly paying the highest price.
"How can I know if this relationship is God's will?"
"Does this relationship make me love Jesus more?"
Because if someone constantly pulls you away from obedience...
or weakens your devotion to Christ...
that is not love leading you closer to life.
Love never asks you to sacrifice your relationship with God.
"You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind." (Matthew 22:37)
The Greek word καρδία (kardia) refers not merely to emotion but to the very center of one's inner life—mind, will, affections, and desires. Genuine love for God encompasses the whole person.
Only when God is loved first can every other relationship find its proper place.
The greatest marriages are not built upon two people staring endlessly into each other's eyes.
They are built upon two sinners looking together toward Christ.
The closer each person walks toward Jesus...
the closer they naturally grow toward one another.
Without Christ, love eventually becomes self-centered.
The greatest proof that love is not blind is the Cross itself.
Jesus saw every sin you would ever commit.
Every moment you would choose yourself over Him.
Yet He still stretched out His hands.
Isaiah foretold this centuries before Christ's birth:
"He was pierced for our transgressions; He was crushed for our iniquities..." (Isaiah 53:5)
The Hebrew word פֶּשַׁע (peshaʿ), translated "transgressions," speaks of deliberate rebellion against rightful authority. Christ did not die merely for accidental mistakes but for willful rebellion.
Perhaps you've spent years believing that your past disqualifies you.
The Gospel never says your scandal is too big.
It says your Savior is greater.
Your scars do not have the final word.
Your regrets do not write the ending.
And when Jesus writes the ending...
grace always has the final chapter.
If this message exposed something hidden in your heart, don't hide it any longer.
Not to shame them, but because truth spoken in love can become the turning point of an entire life.
Feelings change. Christ remains the same.

Every share places the Gospel before people who may never walk into a church but may stop long enough to read a story that points them to Jesus. You may never know this side of eternity whose life God chooses to change through a single act of obedience.
If you desire to glorify God through this ministry, partnering with us is one practical way to participate in spreading His truth.
One soul reached with the Gospel is worth more than a thousand unnoticed scrolls.
